title: Gravitational-Wave Signatures of Compact Extra Dimensions and Their Detectability with Third-Generation Interferometers
content: We investigate gravitational-wave dynamics in theories of gravity formulated in $D=4+N$ dimensions, with matter localized on a four-dimensional brane or coupled to the effective four-dimensional metric obtained after compactification. We consider four representative geometries, i.e., Ricci-flat compactifications $M_4 \times X_N$ with Calabi--Yau manifolds as a string-motivated subclass, warped compactifications with a finite extra-dimensional interval represented by the Randall--Sundrum I (RS1) model, and warped compactifications with a noncompact extra dimension represented by the Randall--Sundrum II (RS2) model. These examples cover the principal spectral structures relevant to gravitational-wave phenomenology. Their effects may become detectable through virtual corrections to the source dynamics. We discuss modifications of binary dynamics, propagation, quasinormal modes, damping, and polarization content. Finally, we formulate a Fisher-matrix framework for future interferometric detectors, such as the Einstein Telescope. The forecast is separated into effective-field-theory corrections, genuine dispersive propagation when a light propagating mode or a continuum response is present, modified black-hole dynamics and quasinormal modes, and radion-induced scalar polarization.
